name: Alpe d'Huez
description: Alpe d'Huez is the Oisans valley's flagship resort. Known for: the Sarenne (16km black run, longest in Europe), the 21-hairpin Tour de France road, and its 250km linked domain including Vaujany, Oz-en-Oisans, and Auris. The resort itself is purpose-built at 1,860m on a sun-exposed plateau. Two sectors: Pic Blanc (3,330m — glacier, Sarenne, off-piste) and Les Grandes Rousses (2,700m, wooded intermediate terrain). Family-friendly with excellent beginner zones.

overview.atmosphere: Legendary 16km Sarenne black run, historic Tour de France stage, family-friendly, 2 ski areas (Alpe d'Huez + Vaujany/Oz/Auris). Biggest resort in the Oisans.

when_to_go.north_facing_slopes: South/south-west facing — excellent sun. Known as 'Ile au Soleil' (Island of Sun).

best_restaurants: La Cime des Neiges (gastronomic, mountain view terrace)

ski_area.beginners_note: Dedicated beginner zones at Alpe d'Huez and Bergers area.

off_piste.off_piste_detail: Grandes Rousses and Pic Blanc off-piste. Guide recommended (Bureau des Guides de l'Oisans).

villages.name: Alpe d'Huez
villages.character: Main resort, purpose-built but with alpine character, sun terrace restaurants, lively apres

honest_drawbacks: Resort architecture is 1960s/70s — functional but not charming
Sarenne run requires shuttle back — 30 min bus ride
Long transfer from Grenoble (1h30 — mountain road)
